stem: Which statement about febrile status epilepticus is most accurate?

options.text: It usually occurs in older school-aged children with repeated previous seizures
It occurs in about 5% of children with febrile seizures and is usually a first seizure in a very young child
It is mainly associated with very high temperature at the time of seizure
It is strongly linked to immediate complete recovery and no predisposing factors
It is defined as any febrile seizure lasting more than 1 minute

explanation: Febrile status epilepticus occurs in about 5% of children with febrile seizures and is usually the first seizure in a very young child. The other options do not match the described epidemiology or features.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Seizures - Emergency Management

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because it is described as occurring in very young children and is usually the first seizure, not a condition of older children with repeated previous seizures.
optionExplanations.B: Correct because it occurs in about 5% of children with febrile seizures and is usually a first seizure in a very young child.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because the notes do not describe it as being mainly associated with very high temperature at the time of the seizure.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because the notes do not present it as having no predisposing factors or as causing immediate complete recovery.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because that is not the definition given in the notes; the correct description is about its frequency and typical presentation in very young children.
